rows.feature: Physics Staff and its Tab key
rows.how: The Creative Physics Staff (left-click locks a ship in place, right-click toggles dragging it, Tab while dragging rotates it, scroll changes the distance) is creative-only and hidden in JEI, so the Tab "Physics Staff Rotate Mode" key does nothing in survival; Simulated's Scroll Up/Scroll Down keys are unbound alternatives

Mechanical crafting (buttons, a redstone transmitter, gold sheets, a precision mechanism). Holding it, right-click a Redstone Link receiver, then press any key: that key now powers the link's frequency (26 keys and more). Right-click the placed typewriter to take control: your movement keys and bound keys drive the links instead of you; right-click again to stop. Sneak + right-click opens its key list; right-click it with a Linked Controller to copy that controller's frequencies. Bindings survive breaking it; a Display Link can show its "Typed Text"

Seated on a ship, F5 also cycles to "Contraption Camera" and "Unlocked Contraption Camera" (the view turns with the ship); scroll to zoom (sub_level_zoom_sensitivity in sable-client.toml) (unverified how it combines with Shoulder Surfing's F5)
With a Navigator route pinned to your HUD, R opens its options: show details, remove the overlay, narrator announcements on/off, toast notifications on/off, overlay GUI scale, screen corner

rows.feature: Fill every part of a copycat (Left Alt)
rows.how: Hold Left Alt while right-clicking a multi-part copycat (double slabs, bytes, byte panels, half panels, boards...) with a block to give every part that material at once. Left Alt is shared with Relics' ability menu and Create's toolbox key
Vertical item vault (iron sheet, barrel, iron sheet); stacks upward like vaults. Craft an item vault alone to get a silo, and back
Horizontal fluid tank (copper sheets + barrel; a fluid tank crafted alone converts). Wrench cycles its window style. Works as a boiler but weaker (heat x0.5, stress x0.8125)

Brass casing, chute, electron tube (makes 2). Put it against a chest or vault: funnels, arms and pipes on the port reach that inventory as if touching it (tight spaces); several ports per inventory; ports can't chain; redstone switches one off. Adds no storage

Two access ports crafted together. Touches two inventories at once: a funnel or arm on it reaches both; its two filter slots decide which side items go to (and come from); filtered-out items are also hidden from Stock Link networks; redstone disables it
Containers in all 16 colors that join into multiblock storage like Create's item vaults

Right-click a Fluid Hatch with a Block of Experience to make it. On a tank: right-click to pour your XP in as liquid, sneak + right-click to take it back; its panel sets how much per click; its filter slot lets it treat another mod's XP fluid the same way

Copper ingot + item drain. Put it on a Create fluid tank: right-click with a bucket or bottle to empty it into the tank (if it can't, it fills your container instead); sneak + right-click fills your container first

Backpack upgrade: mechanical press, depot, andesite casing, brass casing, upgrade base. Put an item in its left slot: the pressed result appears on the right after half a second, no rotation needed (unverified whether skill-gated pressing recipes are refused here as they are in a real press)

Backpack upgrade: mixer, basin, fluid tank, blaze burner, upgrade base. Up to 4 ingredients on the left; its basin takes fluid from the backpack's Tank Upgrade (one button pulls a bucket, another toggles auto-refill); right-click its burner with fuel or use the fuel slot; superheating fuel (blaze cake) turns it blue for superheated recipes

Place a Sophisticated Backpack on a contraption or train: contents, upgrades (pickup, magnet, feeding, filter, void...) and settings keep working while it moves, using the contraption's position; backpacks in schematics keep their colors

Copycats are made from zinc ingots (JEI shows each shape; many convert into each other by crafting). Right-click a placed copycat with a full block to take its look, right-click again with it to rotate or cycle the shape; a wrench takes the material back out. Shapes: block, slab (vertical too), stairs and vertical stairs, slope, vertical slope, slope layer, layer, half layer (vertical, stacked), slice (vertical, corner), byte, byte panel, half panel, board, box, catwalk, beam, vertical step, fence, wall, pane, flat pane, ladder
Right-click a placed layer, half layer or slice with the same copycat item to grow it (slices come in 8 sizes), up to a full block

Double slabs, bytes (8 to a block), byte panels, half panels, half layers and boards hold a different material in each part of one block space; boxes and catwalks (pre-assembled boards) come apart board by board

All copycats connect textures with each other on matching faces; on those whose tooltip has "CT Toggle" (doors and others), sneak + right-click with an empty hand turns it off or on (sliding and folding doors per half)

Copycat doors (plain, iron, sliding, folding), trapdoors (plain, iron), fence gates, ladders, fluid pipes (and glass pipes), shafts and cogwheels (small and large) work like the originals but wear any block's look; the copycat kinetics add no stress

In andesite, zinc, iron, industrial iron, copper and brass: catwalks (with railings and stairs; they place along a line like Create's placement helpers), supports and support wedges, hull plating, sheet metal, mesh fences, bars (plain and paneled), windows and panes, doors, trapdoors, ladders
Eight colors (red, scarlet, blue, umber, dean, dusk, verdant, pearl) as short, long, tiled and corner bricks, cracked and mossy, with stairs, slabs and walls
Placing Create Deco blocks pays 15 Construction XP a block; the Mason's Palette at Construction 99 includes them

Nugget + light source + sheet of the metal: torch gives yellow, soul torch blue, redstone torch red, glow berries green. A placed lamp is dark until the block it hangs on gets a redstone signal; right-click it with an empty hand to invert it (glows without power, goes dark when powered)
Placards (Create's item-display frame) in 16 colors; craft a dyed placard with white dye to get a plain one back (the pack repaired this recipe)
Craft a Create Deco metal door with a redstone torch: the Locked door only opens by redstone, like an iron door; the unlocked metal doors open by hand (unverified in game)
Warning and arrow plates (fire, electrical, skull, no entry, radioactive, arrows...) stonecut from iron sheets
Liquid Dye (mix a dye with water) flowing into lava makes concrete of that color, like a cobblestone generator
Sandpaper (and bulk sanding, the Mechanical Grindstone) also polishes stone into its polished form, scrapes oxidation off copper blocks and removes wax

Right-click envelopes and symmetric sails with dye to paint them; wash dyed envelopes back to white with a fan through water. Nameplates, handles and portable engines come in 16 colors from the crafting table
Throw any music disc high into the clouds and it turns into the Cloud Skipper disc

Lever + 2 andesite alloy + andesite casing. Glue the build into one group (Super Glue or Honey Glue; blocks touching only at an edge count too) with the assembler in it, then hold right-click on its lever and drag to assemble: the build becomes a free-moving physics body. Ponder (W) shows every step

Spout 500 mB of honey onto an iron sheet. Click two corners to glue a box (honey glue range 48 in the server config); Ctrl + scroll grows or shrinks it; hold Alt to place a corner in mid-air. It only sticks for physics ships, not ordinary Create contraptions; on assembly it takes in overlapping Super Glue, not the other way round

Any Physics Assembler on the ship turns it back into blocks (hold and drag the lever), but not in mid-air ("Too far from the ground"), not while moving faster than about 5 blocks a second or spinning, and only if it can line up with the grid: land and stop first

Parts that lose their connection split off into their own body (and fall). Merge two ships with a slime ball: click a face on each (within 4 blocks; not two upward or two downward faces, not a side to a top)
Everything aboard keeps working: walk the deck, open chests, run machines, fans and engines. A ship with a player on it doesn't unload; ships show up to 320 blocks away

Hot Air Envelopes (2 wool + 2 sticks make 4; a deployer pressing a stick into wool makes 3 per wool) build an airtight balloon (plain wool is airtight too); a gap leaks ("Balloon leaks"). A Hot Air Burner (iron sheets, coal block, andesite alloy, redstone) under it needs no fuel: it burns only while it has a redstone signal, the signal strength scales its output up to the max set on its panel. Balloons fill from the top, blocks inside take up volume, several burners can share a balloon; goggles show volume and lift; a soul-infused item changes its flame
Lift from hot air and steam, and propeller thrust, weaken as you climb, so a ship settles where lift equals its weight; turn the burner signal up or down to climb or sink
Right-click a shaft with an envelope to encase it: the balloon stays airtight and the shaft still turns (envelope-encased shafts are made this way, so JEI hides them)
Gold sheet on a copper block. Lift from a boiler's steam: needs heat, water and boiler space like a steam engine; redstone-controlled like the burner; several vents need a higher boiler level

Crush end stone into End Stone Powder; mix 4 powder + 2 zinc nuggets + 500 mB water over a heated basin into Levitite Blend; pour it where you want the block and set it off with flint and steel, a fire charge, a torch or a campfire (torches and campfires aren't used up), or have a campfire, magma block, torch, lit blaze burner or fire nearby, or netherrack or a coal block touching it. The whole pool crystallizes; clay, mud, packed mud and coarse dirt molds break away; a soul torch or soul campfire gives pink Pearlescent Levitite. Enough levitite keeps a ship afloat but can't make it climb, and it drags hard at low speed. End stone comes from the End, or from Dragons Plus (Bulk Ending, dragon's breath + lava)

Propeller Bearing (wooden slab, iron sheet, brass casing) turns whatever is attached in front into a propeller if it has at least 2 sail-like blocks (more sails, more thrust). Reverse thrust by reversing the rotation or with a wrench; thrust falls as the ship speeds up; goggles show thrust, airflow and what it can lift. Andesite and Wooden Propellers are one-block props

Gyroscopic Propeller Bearing (needs a Gyroscopic Mechanism, sequenced assembly) keeps its rotor upright, for helicopters; facing down it steadies a top-heavy ship; a redstone signal resets its tilt. Smart Propeller (makes 2) pitches on one axis to try to face up; wrench reverses it
On a moving ship, ordinary sails give lift across their face (planes, gliders); Symmetric Sails give only drag (fins, rudders, stabilizers) and make windmills without glue

Large cogwheel, andesite casing, shaft. Hold right-click on it and move the mouse to turn; sneak to snap to 45° steps; its panel sets the max angle. It outputs rotation for bearings or wheel mounts (set bearings to not disassemble); a comparator reads the angle, one on its back reads whether someone is steering; right-click with planks to change its wood
Stick on brass casing. Right-click and drag to set a 0-15 analog signal; a wrench inverts it. Feed it to burners (lift) or an analog transmission (propeller speed)
Burns furnace fuel for rotation aboard, no boiler; set its direction; funnels can feed fuel; a Blaze Cake superheats it for more power; goggles show burn time

Iron or copper handles (16 colors). Hold right-click to grab one and swing yourself around it; sneak + hold to drag the ship by it instead; scroll while holding to change the distance; grabbing one can break a long fall
Right-click to type the ship's name; right-click with dye to recolor the text; honeycomb locks it; every nameplate on a ship shares its name; a Display Link can show it

Mechanical crafting, makes 2. Power a pair with redstone to extend them: they line up and lock rigidly while each ship stays its own body; items, fluids and electricity (FE) then pass through (insert on one side, extract on the other); retract either one to undock; a comparator reads docking progress

Rope Coupling (string + iron nuggets): right-click a Rope Winch and a Rope Connector with it to tie them (two winches can't link; up to 40 blocks). Turning the winch reels in or out; shears cut it; right-click the rope holding a wrench to slide down it (a zipline; refuses past 85°)
Connect two blocks with a spring (suspension, bouncy links); wrench right-click sets its strength; right-click with a spring lengthens it, sneak + right-click shortens it

Like a mechanical bearing, but the glued group in front becomes its own physics body on a joint (turrets, doors, landing gear); rotation passes through its shaft; redstone unlocks it to swing freely (behavior set on its panel)

Wheel Mount (andesite casing, a Spring, iron sheet) + a tire (dried kelp around a shaft; Small, standard, Large or Monstrous): right-click the tire onto the mount's front face. Turning the mount drives the wheel; redstone into its top brakes, into a side steers toward that side; scroll its panel for suspension strength

Mechanical crafting. Fire two plungers at blocks: the rope between them pulls the two together (towing, mooring); sneak + right-click clears them; with a backtank on it uses air instead of durability (server config: 100 shots, 64-block range)
Punching a light ship pushes it; shovels act as paddles: hit the water beside a floating build to push it along (unverified exact behavior)
A waystone placed on a ship works and travels with it (shown with [SubLevel] in the warp list); warp plates on ships work too
Right-click it while on a ship to show the forces on it (lift, thrust, gravity, drag arrows), its center of mass and total mass; "Configure Diagram" merges or hides the arrows

Every block has a mass and friction (light to absurdly heavy, slippery, sticky, bouncy, fragile, floating, airtight); heavy hulls need more lift. Tooltips show the values while you wear goggles; Create filters can match "mass is ..." and "friction is ..."
A Create nozzle on an encased fan aboard a ship pushes the ship away from nearby surfaces, water included: hovercraft

Brass sheet, precision mechanism, brass casing. Put a navigation item in it and it outputs redstone toward the target (weaker the further you face away): compass (world spawn), recovery compass (where you last died), lodestone compass, explorer and treasure maps (villages, temples, monuments, mansions, trial chambers, buried treasure), a redstone magnet. A Display Link shows distance and ETA

Navigator (mechanical crafting): right-click to search a train route between two stations (button for your nearest station, swap button); results list departures, transfers, platforms and real-time delays; search settings: fastest or fewest transfers, minimum transfer time, train categories, direct only; save routes
Choose a route to pin it as a HUD overlay: next stop, transfers, toasts for delays, platform changes, cancelled trains and missed connections; optional narrator announcements

In the navigator's global settings: Station Tags merge stations into one multi-platform station (so transfers work), train categories and train lines, station and train blacklists (freight). Everyone can edit these on this server (permission level 0); the mod has owner locks (Unlocked, Trusted players, Locked; ownership transfer) (unverified which entries they cover)

6 from 3 display boards, 4 andesite alloy and 2 sturdy sheets; many shapes (board, small, panel, half panel, sloped, slab, block). Right-click with a wrench to configure: train destination, passenger information (inside trains: next stop, exit side, speed), platform, departure board or static text
Iron sheets, clock, precision mechanism. Right-click it to show the time above your hotbar; right-click it with another clock to make a four-sided clock
Put a Navigator on a lectern for a public route planner at a station (unverified)
Rare loot in Let The Adventure Begin chests: the Grot Explorer Map, King's Castle Explorer Map and Explorer Map lead to those structures
Mechanical crafting. Takes potato cannon ammo (by hand or funnel); rotation charges it, a redstone pulse fires, a steady signal fires automatically; goggles show ammo, damage and reload
Mechanical crafting. With a redstone signal it zaps every player and mob within 3 blocks once a second: 1 heart to players (1.5 to mobs) plus Shocked (heavy slowness), 1,000 FE a shot
Crafted from iron wire; hurts anything moving through it (2 damage)
A Copycat Ghost Block looks like any block but has no collision: hidden doorways and fake walls

Copper sheets, gold ingots, barrel. It breaks on impact and splashes its fluid up to 8 blocks: lava sets fire, potions apply their effect, milk clears effects, water puts out fire, dye colors, dragon's breath hurts, explosive fluids explode (more fluid, stronger effect). Levitite version: 8 tanks around a levitite blend bucket
There are no claims: anyone can board, steer or disassemble your ship (any Physics Assembler on it works), and breaking hull blocks can split it in flight; guard it or hide it
A sprinkler fed with a potion fluid gives that effect to whoever stands under it, lava burns them, liquid experience gives them XP
Boss of Let The Adventure Begin's King's Castle: a 200 HP evoker in goggles holding a Totem of Undying (it has to die twice), with a boss bar and its own loot (unverified what starts the fight)

Cogwheel, andesite casing, turntable. Right-click it with a knife or axe to fit the tool; it runs Farmer's Delight cutting-board recipes on a depot or belt below, and over a basin; it wears the tool down and must spin the right way

rows.feature: Mixer cooking is mostly refused here
rows.how: Slice & Dice adds cooking-pot recipes to a mechanical mixer over a heated basin, but this pack's mixer refuses anything that needs a Cooking level (soups at 10, stews and rice at 20, pasta at 30, feasts...), so only ungated pot recipes work there

Copper sheets, fluid pipe, iron bars (makes 3). Pipe a fluid in from above: water makes the area below count as rained on (5 blocks around), liquid fertilizer bone-meals it; works on moving contraptions and ships; holds 300 mB, 100 mB a spray; craft it to swap ceiling and floor versions
Mix organic compost + 250 mB water (or tree fertilizer + 500 mB water) into Liquid Fertilizer; spout 500 mB onto organic compost to make rich soil

Packagers unpack a recipe's ingredients straight into a cooking pot (factory gauges can order them); mechanical arms put bowls and containers in and take food out; funnels pull cooked food too; arms also load skillets and stoves. A pot fed this way cooks at the Cooking level of whoever last opened it
A blaze burner (or any boiler heater) counts as heat under cooking pots and skillets and speeds them up by heat level
A mechanical saw, or a deployer holding a knife, does Farmer's Delight cutting recipes on belts and depots; arms can put ingredients on a cutting board
Mechanical arms take servings from placed feasts and slices from pies; the last serving stays until a fresh whole one replaces it (feasts need Cooking 50 to make)
Stripping logs in a mechanical saw also gives Farmer's Delight tree bark (straw from bamboo)
Sheep and other mobs (with their armor) that walk through a coloring fan stream or touch Liquid Dye are dyed

Needs a Control Chip (sequenced assembly on a golden sheet with an electron tube, redstone and a press, 3 loops). Right-click to program: Output for a time, Output until a state / exact / min / max input, Transform (a formula with I = input and C = constant), Loop, Loop X times, Loop if..., End. A signal at its back starts it, one at a side stops and resets it; a comparator reads its progress

Craft a Redstone Link into one (and back). Right-click a lever, button or analog lever with it to make that block a wireless transmitter (a Simulated throttle lever too: a wireless throttle); set the frequency with its two item slots; wax with honeycomb against misclicks, an axe to edit again, a wrench to detach; 128-block range
Transmitter + crafter slot cover; placed in a link's frequency slot it matches any item
The Inverted Clutch passes rotation only while powered; the Inverted Gearshift reverses unless powered. Craft a normal clutch or gearshift alone to convert
Powered, it adds 16,384 SU of stress and stalls the whole network at once (an emergency stop). Its recipe uses obsidian, a Hardness III material, so crafting it needs Mining 30
Uncouples after a set delay when its network is overstressed (a circuit breaker); fix the network, then reset it with a wrench or a redstone pulse
Stores an analog signal: input at its back raises it, inputs at its sides lower it, at a rate set on its panel (steps up to an hour long): counters, long timers, analog memory
Its output slides toward its input over time (rate on its panel, up to an hour; copy or invert mode): delays and smooth ramps
Signal by height; set the min and max altitude in its screen or invert it; goggles (or a wrench) show exact height and air pressure
Signal from its tilt, each axis separately (out of the downhill side by default); panels set the full-signal angle and invert it: self-leveling ships
Signal by speed along its facing; set the full-signal speed; output away from or toward the motion
Casts a beam up to 15 blocks: signal strength by the distance to the first block it hits; a filter limits it to matching blocks; works on the ground too

A powered Laser Pointer shines a beam up to 100 blocks (max length set on its back); a Laser Sensor hit by it outputs a signal by laser power; filters match laser colors; wrench on the front or back inverts; any block breaks the beam (tripwires, signals between ships)
Powered magnets attract opposite poles, repel like poles and try to line up: contact-free couplings and docking guides

Receive a Redstone Link frequency by angle (Directional: full straight ahead, weaker off-axis, nothing from behind) or by distance (Modulating: full inside its min range, nothing past its max, proportional between): homing and proximity triggers
A redstone-controlled gear ratio: unpowered it's an encased cogwheel; a signal slows the cog relative to the shaft (or speeds the shaft when driven from the cog); full signal disconnects them
Unpowered it passes nothing; power one side to drive forward, the other to reverse, both to stop: forward, neutral and reverse from two levers
Passes rotation only within a set angle and springs back when the input stops; redstone holds it in place; a comparator reads its angle

Railway casing + eye of ender (eyes need Brewing 55 to craft) makes 2. On a track it makes trains route around it by its penalty value (set with a wrench); redstone from above or below weakens it (full strength switches it off), a comparator reads it; it gives a redstone signal from its sides when a train passes, like a train observer
Electricity passes from its input connector to its output only while it's powered
Copycat buttons (wood, stone) and pressure plates (wood, stone, light and heavy weighted) work as normal but look like any block: hidden switches and traps
Wrench each face to set its rotation direction on its own; a vertical version by crafting
Corner outputs keep their direction, straight-through ones reverse (vertical version by crafting)
Shafts on all six faces; top and bottom turn at half speed
Two separate rotations cross through one block
A chain drive with a cogwheel: every shaft in the chain turns the same way and cogwheels mesh anywhere along it
The Centrifugal Clutch connects only above a set RPM; the Freewheel Clutch only for the direction you set
A one-time connector that snaps when the network overstresses, protecting the rest
Passes a fixed stress capacity (set on its panel) from one network to another while keeping them separate; an overstressed source network stops it (an Overstress Clutch in front frees that capacity)

8 per craft (precision mechanism, brass casing, iron sheets, redstone). Unpowered it charges from rotation at its front; powered it discharges at 64 RPM, spending only what the load needs (none while other sources cover it). Holds 512 su-hours and keeps its charge as an item: right-click a discharging battery with a charged one to swap (deployers and arms automate it); chain front-to-back for longer runs, side by side for more power; read it with a comparator, threshold switch or Display Link; crafting one alone empties it
Hand crank + cogwheel (large version too): hold right-click to turn it counter-clockwise, sneak + hold for clockwise
Moves up to 64 items at a time (4 from brass sheets and a brass ingot)

Empty Fan Catalyst (brass ingots + iron bars), then right-click it (or deploy) with a lava bucket (blasting), water bucket (washing), netherrack (smoking), soul sand (haunting), powder snow bucket (freezing), sand (sanding) or a dragon head (ending), or spout lava, water, dragon's breath or liquid dye into it. Put it in front of an encased fan for bulk processing that never spreads fire or flows; craft it alone to empty it

Crafting a part alone turns it into its sibling: gearbox to 6-way or parallel gearbox, clutch and inverted clutch, gearshift and inverted gearshift, horizontal and vertical gearboxes, item vault and item silo, fluid tank and fluid vessel, Redstone Link and Linked Transmitter

Sequenced Gearshift gains Loop, Sustain (turn until the next pulse) and Turn-for-time; Attribute Filters gain "has the word ... in ID", "has X max durability" and "stacks to N"; schematics can sit in sub-folders (5 deep); jukeboxes and note blocks on contraptions answer contraption controls
A fan through powder snow (or a freezing catalyst): ice to packed ice to blue ice, blaze rod to breeze rod, magma cream to slime ball
A fan through a dragon head or dragon's breath: cobblestone to end stone (powder for levitite), stone bricks to end stone bricks, apple to chorus fruit, leather to phantom membrane
Mix a dye with water into Liquid Dye (heated mixing turns it back into dye); a fan through it dyes items in bulk (anything with a dye crafting recipe)
Needs quicksand, which this pack doesn't have; a Fan Sanding Catalyst (empty catalyst + sand) gives the same bulk sandpaper processing

An item drain empties dragon's breath bottles into fluid and a spout refills them; it works in cauldrons and drips through pointed dripstone into a cauldron below (renewable); flowing into lava it makes end stone

Fan streams from ships act on the world: washing puts out fire, freezing freezes water, blasting spreads fire to flammable blocks, coloring dyes blocks (smoking, haunting, ending and sanding don't; unverified exactly which blocks each changes)
Mechanical crafting. Turns rotation into electricity (FE); needs at least 32 RPM; output rises with RPM (75% efficient)
Mechanical crafting. Turns electricity into rotation: scroll its back panel to set the RPM (up to 256); higher RPM draws more power (at least 8 FE/t)

Small Connector (copper rod, andesite alloy, slime ball; makes 3): Copper Spool, up to 4 links, 16 blocks, 1,000 FE/t. Large Connector: Gold or Electrum Spool, 6 links, 32 blocks, 5,000 FE/t. Right-click two connectors with a spool to wire them (the spool isn't used up); an Empty Spool on two linked connectors takes the wire back; a wrench cycles Push, Pull and None; the Small Connector With Light glows when powered; "Wire is too long" means too far

Multiblock battery up to 3 wide and 5 tall (2,000,000 FE a block); give it one input and one output connector; it also pushes power into blocks on its top and bottom; a Display Link shows its charge (percent, bar)
Rolls ingots and plates into rods and wires (spools, connectors and motors need them); drop items on top, right-click to take the output; a belt and two funnels automate it
Right-click a blaze burner with Straw: it then takes liquid fuel by bucket or pipe (lava, biofuel, seed oil) for steady heat with no solid fuel
Compact seeds into seed oil; mix plants, leaves, saplings or flowers into biomass and compact it into biomass pellets (a strong solid fuel); mix bioethanol (biofuel)

Brass casing, chute, copper spool. Swaps power with accumulators on a passing contraption or train (1-2 block gap, like a portable storage interface); redstone stops it engaging; trains can wait for the "Energy Cargo" schedule condition
Charges electric items below it; charging recipes: gold (ingot, sheet, nugget, wire...) to electrum, oxidized copper blocks back one stage, a book into a Channeling book (1,000,000 FE)
Crush a diamond into diamond grit; the sandpaper lasts 1,024 uses

1 experience nugget = 3 mB, a Block of Experience = 27 mB (compacting 27 mB makes a block), a Bottle o' Enchanting drains to 10 mB (a spout refills bottles). Liquid XP poured in the world turns into orbs, and a broken pipe sprays orbs

Right-click an Item Drain with a Mechanical Grindstone (andesite alloy around a shaft) to turn it into a Grindstone Drain (JEI hides it because it's made this way), then put a Mechanical Grindstone on top: it disenchants gear into liquid XP, grinds experience nuggets and blocks into liquid XP, and polishes like sandpaper (unverified exact layout beyond the Ponder)
The smithing template behind the blaze machines: the first one comes from Nether fortress and bastion chests; copy it with 7 blaze rods and a netherrack (makes 2)

Smithing table: Blaze Upgrade template + blaze burner + enchanting table (Enchanting 35 to make; the table needs Crafting 40). Pipe in liquid XP; set the enchanting level on its panel (max 30, while the pack's own table reaches 150 with Enchanting); put an item in the panel's filter to roll only that item's enchantments (template mode, which fills Enchanting Templates); mechanical arms feed it and take the results

Smithing table: Blaze Upgrade template + blaze burner + anvil (no skill gate). With liquid XP it works like an anvil with no repair cost: merges two of the same item or book, merges templates, applies an Enchanting Template to an item, strips enchantments from gear or books onto a blank template
Press a Block of Experience into a blank Enchanting Template; fill it with enchantments in a blaze enchanter in template mode, then stamp it onto item after item in a blaze forger

Feed an enchanter or forger a Cake o' Enchanting (compact egg + sugar + lapis into a cake base, spout 1,000 mB liquid XP on it): it seethes and takes only Super Enchanting Templates, pressed from Blocks of Super Experience (a Block of Experience struck by lightning; the server config has every natural strike convert it, so a lightning rod in a thunderstorm works). It gives treasure enchantments and merges conflicting ones, but in this pack never raises a level past the skill caps. Keep a lightning rod nearby: covering the machine instead risks curses or repair cost

Brass sheet, spout, iron block (Enchanting 50 to make). Put what to print in its filter and pipe in the fluid: copies written books, enchanted books (costs liquid XP), train schedules, clipboards and other Create copyables, renames items, changes package addresses and patterns, prints banner patterns with dye. Books with Hardness can't be copied. JEI lists every printing recipe

Block of experience, sponge, copper casing. Pulls XP orbs from 10 blocks around and drains XP from players near it, glowing as it fills (works on contraptions): a mob-farm collector; don't stand next to someone else's
Mobs a deployer kills drop XP and deployers collect it as nuggets; Mending on a deployer's tool repairs it from that XP; deployers can sweep-attack; crushing wheel kills drop XP 30% of the time

Moves items along a powered shaft (wrench swaps shaft and cog, industrial iron encases it, goggles show the flow); on a contraption it collects the drops of drills, saws and harvesters connected beside it; nothing goes in or out at its ends or the cog

New schedule entries: Train Separation (space trains evenly), Prioritized Destination (next free station from a list; can avoid red signals and occupied stations, with a detour limit), Travel Section (starts a section and sets the train line), Dynamic Delay
Hidden veins (at most one per chunk) that never run out: find one with a vein finder, drill it with a drilling machine

Overworld: coal, copper, iron, gold, zinc, lapis, redstone (raw redstone crushes into 4 redstone), water; Nether: quartz, glowstone, nether gold. Each kind turns up about once per 128 by 128 chunk region (2,048 blocks across); water veins about four times as often, nether gold a quarter as often (from the vein placement data; unverified in game); no diamond, emerald or netherite veins in this pack

Right-click: "Found in Chunk" (you're on one), "Found nearby" (next chunk) or "Found traces of" a farther vein with a rough distance; 5 s cooldown; an Ore Vein Atlas in your inventory with a target set makes it report only that kind. Recipe: eye of ender, amethyst shard, a redstone ore block, 2 sticks: eyes of ender need Brewing 55 to craft and redstone ore needs Silk Touch plus Mining 20 to use, so get them from a friend or trade

Mechanical crafting (brass blocks, casings, a mechanical drill, precision mechanisms, sturdy sheets...). Places a multiblock that must sit on solid ground over the vein; put a drill head in, give it rotation (192-512 SU by ore) and pull the output from its IO block; higher RPM is faster and the head isn't used up; any number of machines can share a vein

Iron Drill (2 iron blocks + 5 iron ingots; Mining 50 to make) mines every vein left in this pack. Diamond (Mining 65) and Netherite (Mining 80) heads were for the removed veins and, since speed comes from RPM, add nothing here (unverified)
Chest, amethyst, map, book and quill. Records veins: click a finished Sample Drill or a running Drilling Machine with it; in it, set a target vein, exclude or hide others; the finder then follows it
Mechanical crafting. Place it on a found vein with a Copper Backtank (with air) on top, click to start, wait one cycle, then click it with the atlas to record that vein
Like the drilling machine, for water veins: endless water
Raw iron and raw zinc from a vein need Mining 10, raw gold and redstone Mining 20, before you can take them out of a machine by hand or use them; funnels and belts still move them

Borehead Bearing (wooden slab, gearbox, industrial iron block) + Rock Cutting Wheels (attach without glue) + a storage block on the bore: it breaks blocks in a radius around each wheel, turning at a quarter speed in reverse; mining speed comes from RPM; the more it cuts per pass the slower it goes (use several bearings); it stops when the storage is full, so pull items out of the bearing

Structures Arise and Let The Adventure Begin ruins are built from Create blocks you can take apart, and their chests (per player, Lootr) hold Create materials, raw zinc among them (unverified which machines each has)
rows.mod: Create: Structures Arise / Let The Adventure Begin

rows.how: Armor enchantment from Let The Adventure Begin: +1 Luck per level for better chest loot; its cap is raised to X with Enchanting
Boots, up to III: walking now and then gives an XP point while you're below level 30
Mixing a rabbit foot into 250 mB of luck potion gives 500 mB of Luck IV (10 minutes): better loot from chests (unverified where the first luck potion comes from)

Display board on brass casing. A 4-line mini display: a written clipboard sets static text, a Display Link live data, dye and glow ink color it; anyone sitting in front of it sees it on their HUD (a wrench turns that off, an empty hand resets it)

Display Link sources: altitude and air pressure, gimbal angles, speed, optical and laser distance, navigation target distance and ETA, portable engine burn time, ship name, typewriter text, auger throughput; balloon volume and total lift, propeller thrust and airflow; kinetic battery and accumulator charge
rows.mod: Create Simulated, Create Aeronautics, Create: Connected, Crafts & Additions

rows.how: simulated-client.toml: displayProperties (ALWAYS, SHIFT, GOGGLES, SHIFT_GOGGLES, NEVER; default GOGGLES) decides when block mass and friction show in tooltips; steering wheel GUI X/Y offset
Leather + engineer's goggles: the same goggle readouts with an aviator look

Tracked missions show at the top right; brassworksmissions-client.toml (Mods, Brassworks Missions, Config) aligns them left or bottom, offsets them and shrinks them (NORMAL, SMALL, EXTRA_SMALL); they aren't in HUD Layout
createrailwaysnavigator-client.toml: speed unit (km/h by default; m/s, mph, ft/s, knots), 24-hour, 12-hour or ticks, real-time countdowns, overlay scale (0.75), corner (top left), toasts
copycats-client.toml: colorizeMultiStates tints each part of a multi-material copycat so you can tell them apart; useEnhancedModels
H, `/missions` or ESC, Missions: Create-flavored missions that pay Coin Pouches; rerolls cost pouches
6 missions at a time, a new set every Sunday at 00:00 UTC (the screen counts down); scroll the list to pick one
A finished mission pays only when you press Claim Reward in the screen: 1 to 32 Coin Pouches by mission (100 coins each); unclaimed rewards survive the weekly reset

The first two rerolls each week are free, then 2, 4, 6... pouches (2 more each time) up to 32; after the 18th the button locks until Sunday; the pouches must be in your inventory (not a backpack); a completed mission can't be rerolled
Select a mission and press Track/Untrack in the screen to show its progress on the HUD; the Track key is unbound in this pack (T is chat), so bind it in Controls if you want one

Some need skills or gear: mining diamond ore (Hardness III, Mining 30), diamond tools and swords (Crafting 30), mechanical crafting (crafters at Crafting 30), drill, saw and harvester missions (machines at Mining, Woodcutting and Farming 15), elytra flight; reroll those
Mission milestones (10 to 1,000 claimed) are quests in the Mastery group's Contracts
Create Deco's Gold, Iron, Brass, Copper, Zinc, Industrial Iron and Netherite Coins and Coin Stacks are decoration; the server's currency is the Gold Coins vendors pay
Blaze enchanter Enchanting 35, printer Enchanting 50, ore vein drill heads Mining 50, 65 and 80; only making them is gated, anyone can use one
rows.mod: Create: Enchantment Industry, Create Ore Excavation

rows.how: Create Aeronautics has known visual problems with Iris shaders; if ships render wrong, press K to turn shaders off

Options, Sub-Level Settings: physics steps per second (higher is smoother and heavier; unverified whether it matters on a server). sable-client.toml: ship shadows on the world (off), dynamic shading, water occlusion, UDP networking for smoother ship movement
Hold **W** with the mouse over any Create item (inventory, JEI list); the tooltip says "Hold [W] to Ponder". An animated scene shows how it works

In a scene: arrows = previous/next scene for that item, Replay, Think Back (back to the item pondered before), Identify (pauses: hover any block in the scene to read its name), Comfy Reading (slows scenes while text shows); the "Associated Entries" row at the bottom ponders related items

rows.feature: Ponder tags: what works with what
rows.how: The category icons beside a scene (and in the Ponder Index) list every block of a group: Sources for Display Links, Targets for Display Links, Targets for Mechanical Arms, Targets for Threshold Switches, Contraption Actors, Movement Anchors, Sails for Windmill Bearings, Railway Equipment, High Logistics, Fluid Manipulators

Create's own menu button (title screen / pause screen, "Configure..." menu) has "Ponder Index": every scene by category. Where the button lands on the pack's ESC board is unverified (the board puts other mods' buttons in free slots or the tray)
Hold Shift over a Create item for its summary; items with controls also say "Hold [Ctrl] for Controls" (clipboard, wrench, filters, schematic tools, linked controller, toolbox, backtank...)
rows.docs: MISSING (faq.md covers Shift for the pack's own details only)

rows.how: Right-click a Create component with the Wrench to turn it around the face you clicked (shafts, cogs, gearboxes, funnels, chutes, pumps...)

Sneak + right-click with the Wrench dismantles a Create component straight into your inventory, no mining. Also works (tag create:wrench_pickup) on vanilla redstone wire, redstone torches, repeaters, comparators, levers, buttons, pressure plates, observers, pistons, hoppers, redstone lamps, daylight detectors, targets, tripwires, all rails, and on Create's bars, industrial iron and weathered iron blocks

Cyber Goggles (on by default): left-clicking a wrenchable block while holding a wrench dismantles it at once (it sends the same sneak + use). Easy to trigger by accident on your own machines; turn off in \ -> Misc -> Wrench

Bind "Open Block Rotation Menu" (Controls -> Key Binds -> Create; unbound by default). Hold a wrench, look at a Create kinetic block or a hopper, press it: a radial menu sets its Axis / Facing / Target / Vertical directly. Cyber Goggles' "Always Allow Rotating" (on by default, marked "may be considered cheating") works without the wrench and removes the cooldown

The small labelled panel on a block's side (stack size, RPM, delay, mode, direction...): right-click and hold on it, move the mouse to the value or option on the board, release to confirm. Sneak + right-click ignores the panel (to place blocks against it). Cyber Goggles shows every panel's value without a wrench in hand ("Always Show Scroll Value", on)

Hover a number or option in a Create screen and scroll; hold Shift to scroll faster. Cyber Goggles: middle-click a number in the stock keeper, factory gauge, threshold switch or redstone requester screen to type an exact amount

Right-click a block's filter slot with an item: it now filters for that item (a ghost copy, your item is not used). Click with another item to replace it. A List Filter or Attribute Filter put in the slot is taken from you and given back when replaced or when the block is broken
rows.docs: MISSING (create.md: "filters choose which items go where")

rows.how: Hold right-click on the filter slot of a brass funnel, smart chute and similar to choose "Up to N" or "Exactly N" items per transfer (Any = whole stack)

Hold a Clipboard: right-click a block to copy its settings (filter, value boxes), left-click another block of the same kind to paste. Pasting a List/Attribute filter needs that filter item in your inventory (it gets used). Right-click a placed clipboard with yours to copy its entries
Create has separate Shift, Ctrl and Alt modifier keys (Controls -> Create), used for tooltips, Ctrl-scroll in schematic tools and chassis ranges; rebind them apart from Sneak/Sprint if they clash

Hold a shaft, piston pole, girder, metal ladder, sail, display board, table cloth, copycat panel/step, drill, saw, deployer, roller or steam engine and look at one already placed: a ghost shows where the next goes; right-click extends the row, even into the air (up to 12 blocks). Indicator style and size: Mods -> Ponder -> Config -> Placement Assist (TEXTURE / TRIANGLE / NONE)

Cyber Goggles, Tab: looking at an encased cogwheel, encased pipe or chassis with an empty hand shows a tip; hold Tab to toggle the face on the far side instead of the one you look at (empty-hand toggling is a Cyber Goggles option; unverified on the server)
Cyber Goggles: hold Left Ctrl to right-click the world behind a moving contraption instead of the contraption

Cyber Goggles keys "Use Schematic" and "Show Super Glue" (unbound): while held, that item is swapped from your inventory into your hand (e.g. to see glued areas or schematic tools) and back on release
Cyber Goggles key (unbound): in any inventory screen, hover a List, Attribute or Package filter and press it to view its settings without taking it out

Bulk storage: 20 stacks per block; vaults placed together merge (base up to 3x3, length up to 3x the width, so 3x3x9 = 1,620 stacks) into one inventory. No GUI: fill and empty it with funnels, chutes, arms, an Item Hatch or packagers; a comparator reads its fill
Place it on a container (chest, barrel, vault...). Right-click it with an item to deposit that stack; sneak + right-click to dump your whole inventory except the hotbar into the container
Holds 8 item types, up to 4 stacks each; keeps its contents when broken; dye it any colour. No owner lock: any player within 10 blocks can use a toolbox, and funnels/hoppers can empty it

Within 10 blocks of a placed toolbox hold Left Alt: a radial menu; pick an item to put it in your hand (the slot stays linked to the box). Open the menu again to "Return items to Toolbox", "Return items to nearby Toolboxes", unequip, or "Stop tracking and keep item"; out of range you are told. (Relics' Active Abilities Menu is also on Left Alt: rebind one if they clash, unverified)
Middle-click (Pick Block) a block you don't carry while a toolbox is in range: the item is pulled from the toolbox into your hand

Put a Packager on each storage block and a Stock Link on each packager; right-click a link with a Stock Ticker before placing it, then seat a mob or blaze burner in front of the ticker (it becomes the Stock Keeper). Right-click the keeper: search everything in the linked storage, click items to add them, set an address and Send; they come out packaged where the address leads

Its search box and JEI's are synced both ways (Create client config syncRecipeViewerSearch = SYNC_BOTH); JEI's + on a recipe fills the order with its ingredients. Cyber Goggles: Left Alt + click orders all of an item, middle-click types an amount, "Auto Replenish" (schematic mode) orders the ingredients of missing checklist items in one click
Right-click the Stock Ticker itself to open the category editor; a List or Attribute filter in a category decides which items it groups

Attach to an inventory: a redstone pulse packs its items into a Cardboard Package; packages put into it are unpacked into the inventory (it refuses ones it can't fully unpack). A sign on the packager sets the address its packages carry

Carry and store them like items (Cyber Goggles tooltips list the contents). Sneak + right-click a held package to open it into your inventory; hold right-click and release to throw it (they land in chutes, belts, frogports)
Right-click to open: lines with checkboxes, several pages, "Erase checked items". Sneak + click to hang it on a block. Cyber Goggles draws its text while held and lets Left Ctrl + scroll flip pages

Hang it on a wall; right-click an empty slot to set a recipe (and the item shown); right-click a set slot to craft it from your inventory, sneak to craft up to a stack. Pack: it asks the clicking player's skill level like a crafting table

Cyber Goggles: hover a shulker box, chest item, toolbox, ender chest (your last-seen contents), backtank, map, list/attribute filter, linked controller, package, placard or table cloth to see what is inside in the tooltip

Right-click two corners of a build (hold Ctrl and scroll to pick a point in mid-air); Ctrl + scroll on a face to grow or shrink the box; right-click again to save and name it (or "Save and Upload Immediately"). Files go to the schematics folder of your game directory

Put an Empty Schematic in, pick a file ("Open Folder", "Refresh Files") to upload it onto the schematic. Server limits: 256 KB per file, the server keeps your last 10. Cyber Goggles adds subfolders, a folder picker, a rotatable 3D preview beside the table, and a preview when you hold Alt over a schematic item

Hold the schematic: a tool bar shows; hold Left Alt (Focus Schematic Overlay) and scroll to pick a tool. Position: right-click the ground (hold Ctrl for a fixed distance, Ctrl + scroll to change it); Move XZ / Move Y / Rotate (90 degrees) / Mirror: Ctrl + scroll while pointing at it. Sneak + right-click to type exact coordinates. Print is creative-only

Put the positioned schematic in its slot and gunpowder in the fuel slot (400 blocks per gunpowder); it takes blocks from inventories next to it; status shows the next missing item. Settings: Don't Replace / Replace with Solid / with Any / with Empty, Skip missing blocks, Protect block entities. Pack: Construction 30 to make
Put a Clipboard or Book in the cannon's Checklist Printer slot: a material list. Hand the printed clipboard to a Stock Keeper to order everything on it from your network

Keep it in your hotbar; right-click a surface to place or move the mirror, sneak + use to set the type (Mirror Once, Rectangular, Octagonal) and orientation, use on nothing to remove it; blocks you place within 50 blocks are mirrored (survival: copies use your blocks, unverified)
Right-click with any full block to take its look; click again to cycle orientation or powered state; a wrench resets it; the panel also takes bars and trapdoors. (Copycats+ adds more shapes)

Cut, polished cut, cut bricks, small bricks, layered and pillar forms (plus slabs, stairs, walls) of andesite, granite, diorite, calcite, dripstone, deepslate, tuff, limestone, scoria, scorchia, crimsite, ochrum, veridium and asurine: stonecutter or an upward Mechanical Saw. Pays Construction XP (10)
Lava meeting Create's honey makes limestone, lava meeting chocolate makes scoria (generators like a cobble generator); scoria also smelts from soul sand
Windows and panes in every wood plus industrial iron and ornate iron; framed, horizontal framed, vertical framed and tiled glass with panes; framed glass doors and trapdoors

Andesite, brass and copper bars, ladders, scaffolding and doors; metal girders (a shaft can run through one); metal and wooden brackets to dress shafts, cogs and pipes; industrial and weathered iron blocks; casings as building blocks; copper shingles and tiles (weather like copper, can be waxed)

Seats, sails, table cloths (plus andesite, brass and copper covers), valve handles, toolboxes, postboxes and nixie tubes come in 16 colours; right-click a placed one with dye to recolour it (belts too); shears turn a sail back into a frame
A brass frame for an item: right-click with an item to show it, punch to take it out; safe on contraptions

Cuckoo Clock: shows the time with rotation, chimes at noon and again at dusk once players can sleep. Flywheel: a big brass wheel that spins. Peculiar Bell placed right above soul fire turns into a Haunted Bell
Hold it or ring it: nearby spots dark enough for hostile mobs to spawn light up; a quick check before lighting a base (also works on a moving contraption)
Use on a sapling: grows the tree even without the usual room (tight builds, tree farms)
Right-click a seat (16 colours) to sit, Left Shift to stand. A seat on a contraption keeps you on board while it moves. Right-click a seat while leading a mob to sit the mob down
Hostile mobs walking past an empty seat sit on it (server default seatHostileMobs = true): mind seats in open areas, or use them to hold mobs

Right-click an existing track (or place one), then place or click a second point: straight runs, turns and slopes up to 32 blocks a time, turns up to 90 degrees, no sloped S-bends. Hold Sprint while connecting for the widest bend. Blocks in your off-hand are paved under the track

Track laid up against a Nether portal makes a paired track on the other side (that portal must exist already); trains then cross dimensions. Pack note (PACK_DESIGN.md): riders can get kicked crossing, so send freight unmanned

Right-click a track with a Train Station to select it, place the station nearby; open it and switch to assembly mode. Use Train Casing on the highlighted track to make bogeys (click again to cycle the design, break the block on top to remove one); build carriages on one or two bogeys and Super Glue them; add a forward-facing Train Controls (a second facing back lets it leave stations both ways); confirm in the station screen. Not on curves or diagonals; the front bogey must be at the station marker; up to 20 bogeys. Pack: Agility 35 to make stations and controls

Right-click the Train Controls: W/S to speed up and brake, A/D to choose the branch at junctions, scroll to set the top speed, hold Space near a station to stop at it, Sprint to blow its whistles, sneak or click again to let go. A driven train goes 75% of a scheduled one's speed
Furnace fuel in chests or barrels on the train makes it faster (top speed 28 to 40 blocks/s, 14 to 20 on turns); fuel kept in vaults on board is not burned

A train turns back into blocks only at a station (station screen, all carriages aligned). Wrench + right-click a train, then click a nearby track to move it there (fixes a derailed train; not while it moves)

Right-click the Train Schedule item to edit. Actions: Travel to Station (* wildcard, e.g. "Mine, Platform *": takes the nearest free match), Limit Max Speed, Update Title, Deliver Package, Retrieve Package. Each action waits on conditions: Scheduled Delay, Time of Day (with repeats), Item / Fluid Cargo, Cargo Idle, Players Seated, Station Powered, Redstone Link, Chunk Unloaded; extra rows are alternatives. Left-click edits, right-click removes; Loop Forever

Right-click a mob or blaze burner sitting in front of the Train Controls with the schedule (seat a mob by leading it to the seat); right-click the conductor with an empty hand to take the schedule back
Put a schedule into a station's screen: it copies itself to every train that stops there; drivers don't keep the item

Select a track, place the signal nearby. Signals cut the line into sections and a scheduled train won't enter an occupied one; trains never pass a signal from behind unless a second signal faces the other way. Wrench: brass "cross" mode, only lets a train in if it can leave the section straight away (keeps junctions clear). Nixie tubes on a signal make it easier to see. Player-driven trains are not held
Scheduled trains keep running where nobody is, stopping at stations and red signals; drills and other actors on board don't work there
In the station screen choose which doors open on arrival (all, north / south / east / west side only, none); Create's doors on trains and elevators slide open by themselves
A Display Link reading a station ("Train Station Summary", with a name filter and column sizes) onto a Display Board makes a live arrivals board

Build the cabin; put a pair of Redstone Contacts facing each other and glue one to the cabin; place an Elevator Pulley above (with rotation) and right-click it to assemble. Each fixed contact in that column becomes a floor (Elevator Contact: give it a name). A redstone pulse at a floor calls the cabin; Contraption Controls in the cabin: scroll and click to pick a floor; doors open and close by themselves; a Desk Bell rings on arrival; right-click the pulley to turn the cabin back into blocks
Right-click a chain conveyor holding a wrench to hang from it and ride the chains; at a junction look at the chain you want
Anyone who steps on a Weighted Ejector is launched to its target (up to 32 blocks, any height, not sideways): up cliffs, across gaps (mind fall damage)
Encased fans push or pull players up to 20 blocks (vertical lifts); moving belts carry players and mobs along. Diving boots make you immune to belts

A powered Cart Assembler on a rail mounts the attached structure on a passing minecart (two assemblers sharing one structure make a two-cart carriage); an unpowered one turns passing cart contraptions back into blocks. Furnace carts refuel from the contraption's chests. Wrench + right-click a cart contraption to pick it up as an item (not if too big or carrying a spawner). Minecart Coupling links carts (2 per cart, up to 32 apart). Value box: always face motion, pause actors while turning, or lock rotation

Copper Diving Helmet + Copper Backtank: water breathing that uses the tank's air. Diving Boots: sink fast, walk and jump on the sea floor, not moved by belts. Netherite helmet + netherite backtank + netherite legs and diving boots: immune to fire and lava, clearer sight in lava, walk lava lake floors. Pack: Defence 5 for the copper set (backtank included), Defence 50 for netherite

Fill a backtank by placing it and driving it with rotation (faster = quicker); a full tank holds 900 s of air, +300 per Capacity level (Capacity goes to X in this pack); the HUD warns "Backtank pressure low"; a comparator reads its fill

rows.feature: Train map on the world map
rows.how: Create draws every track network and live train on Xaero's World Map (M), with a "Train network overlay" toggle on the map. Hover a train for its name, owner, next stop and problems (waiting at signal, derailed, navigation failed, conductor missing, fuel boosted). Everyone sees every train
The station screen sets the train's colour on maps ("Color on Maps") and the station's icon type
Right-click a train station with a map: the map gets a labelled marker there

Right-click: fires the next ammo item from your inventory. Each ammo has its own damage, knockback and reload: potato 5 (plants potatoes where it lands), melon 8, blaze cake 15 and sets the target on fire, chorus fruit teleports the target, pufferfish and poisonous potatoes poison, golden apple cures zombie villagers. Uses durability, or with a backtank worn its air (200 shots a tank). Potato Recovery (up to VII here) reuses ammo. Pack: Ranged 20

Crushing wheels (4 damage a hit), saws, drills, rollers and fan streams through lava or fire hurt and kill players; the death message names whoever knocked them in ("was thrown into a Saw by ..."). Whether that counts as a player kill for lifesteal is unverified
Moving trains damage players and mobs in their way (server default trainsCauseDamage = true); death message "was run over by"

A Cuckoo Clock crafted inside 4 gunpowder looks the same ("Cuckoo Clock") but, while turning, explodes when it chimes: a creeper-sized blast (power 3) that breaks blocks. With no claims, be wary of gifted clocks
Wear the full set of cardboard armor and sneak: you look like a cardboard box. Cyber Goggles removes the box's view blocking for you (on by default)

"Remove Train Damage" (off), "Always Allow Riding Chain" (off), "Enhanced Connection" for chain conveyors (on) and "Always Allow Rotating" (on) are marked "may be considered cheating on server" in its config; leave the off ones off
On a moving contraption: harvests ripe crops and replants them, leaves unripe ones (server defaults); drops go into the contraption's chests. Pack: Farming 15 to make
On a contraption: breaks blocks without a full hitbox (grass, flowers, torches), tills dirt into farmland, and flings mobs without hurting them. Pack: Farming 15 to make
A saw (stationary or on a contraption) that cuts the bottom log fells the whole tree, with bee nests, cocoa, vines, moss carpet and shroomlights on it. Pack: Woodcutting 15 to make
Millstone or crushing: wheat -> wheat flour (+ chance of more and of seeds); washing flour -> dough; dough smelts (or fan-smokes) into bread

A Spout fills items under it: chocolate onto sweet berries = Chocolate Glazed Berries, honey onto an apple = Honeyed Apple, milk onto bread = Sweet Roll, tea into a bottle = Builder's Tea; chocolate is mixed (heated) from sugar, cocoa and milk, tea from leaves, water and milk
A fluid pipe pulling from a bee nest or beehive collects honey (as a fluid)

Fan through soul fire or a soul campfire: red / brown mushroom -> crimson / warped fungus, sweet berries -> glow berries, ink sac -> glow ink sac, potato -> poisonous potato, sand -> soul sand, dirt -> soul soil, cobblestone -> blackstone, brick -> nether brick, torches / lanterns / campfires -> soul versions
Mix 4 bamboo, sugar cane or saplings with 250 mB water into pulp, press it into cardboard (cardboard blocks, cardboard armor and sword)

Wireless redstone: put items in a link's two frequency slots (the pair is the channel); sneak + right-click (or wrench right-click) switches it between transmitter and receiver. Receivers give out the strength their transmitter receives (analog), within 256 blocks

Right-click a receiving Redstone Link with it, then press one of six keys (forward, back, left, right, jump, sneak) to bind that key to the link's channel. Right-click to switch the controller on: those keys now send redstone instead of moving you; right-click again to stop. Sneak + right-click opens its manual setup
Right-click a lectern with a Linked Controller to put it in; use the lectern to drive without holding it; sneak + right-click to take it back
Right-click to raise its output by 1 (0 to 15), sneak + right-click to lower it
A redstone-controlled lever: a signal at its back turns it on, a signal at a side turns it off (RS latch); right-click toggles it
Each signal at its back flips it on or off (T flip-flop); right-click toggles it
Gives one short pulse after a set delay (value box, up to an hour)
Lengthens a signal: turns on after a short delay and stays on for the set time (value box, up to an hour)
Pulses again and again at the set interval (value box); a signal into its input side pauses and resets it; right-click the base to invert it (on except during the pulse)
Two contacts facing each other give a signal, even when one rides a moving contraption (a piston, gantry, bearing or cart has arrived)

Lights on a signal and stays lit (it powers redstone itself). In a connected group, lighting one turns the others off (a selector); a comparator reads how far away the lit lamp is; a wrench toggles one by hand
Shows the redstone strength it receives as digits; right-click with a written Clipboard for custom text, with dye to change its colour; a Display Link target

Shows live information on a display: right-click the display (Display Board, Nixie Tubes, sign, lectern) with the link, then place the link on the block to read from (up to 64 blocks apart); open it to choose what to send. A redstone signal pauses its updates

What a link can read: item or fluid counts and lists in a container, fill level (percent or bar), item throughput per second / minute / hour, rotation speed, network stress, boiler status, time of day, a stopwatch, station arrivals, train schedule status, a passing train's name, elevator floor, factory gauge status, redstone power, a scoreboard, player deaths, max enchanting cost, copies of nixie tubes
A scalable sign: place several side by side; needs at least 30 RPM; right-click a line with a written Clipboard for text, with dye to colour a line, with an empty hand to clear it

Attach to a container, tank, vault or rope pulley; in its screen set "on at or above" and "off at or below" levels: the output holds until the lower level is reached (keeps a buffer topped up); a filter counts only one item; can be inverted

Signals when a container or tank holds the filtered item or fluid, when the block in front matches the filter, while items pass on a belt, chute or pipe it faces; pulses when an item goes through a funnel

A comparator reads: item vault, basin, depot, ejector and toolbox fill; fluid tank, spout and item drain contents; backtank air; blaze burner heat; speedometer and stressometer readings; the sequenced gearshift's step; 15 while a train is at a station; red train signals; 15 while a portable storage interface is docked; packagers, frogports, postboxes, redstone requesters
Dials for rotation speed and network stress; a comparator next to one gives a signal in proportion (e.g. switch machines off near the stress limit)

Right-click to program a list: Turn by angle, Turn to move a piston / pulley / gantry a distance, Delay, Await new redstone pulse, End; each at input or double speed, forward or reversed. A redstone signal starts it; it then waits for the next signal; a comparator reads the current step
Clutch: powered = stops passing rotation; Gearshift: powered = reverses it
A chain drive that, powered, doubles the speed it sends along the chain (halves it if it isn't the source); an analog signal sets any ratio between 1x and 2x

A signal pauses funnels, smart chutes, mechanical arms, deployers, weighted ejectors, display links and portable storage interfaces. Arms and deployers finish their current move first, so a short off-pulse runs exactly one cycle
A powered gantry shaft stops its carriages and passes its rotation to the carriage's output shaft instead
Each redstone signal toggles it: on, the block in front is attached (moves with a contraption); toggle again to let go
Powered: mounts its structure on a passing cart; unpowered: disassembles carts. On powered or controller rail it holds the cart until powered

On a contraption: right-click to switch its actors (drills, saws, deployers...) on or off while moving; while the contraption is still blocks, set its filter to target one actor type; if it is redstone-powered at assembly, the targeted actors start off
A one-way powered rail whose push follows the redstone strength
Right-click a placard with an item: if the same item is already framed it gives a short pulse (an item "key" for doors)
Right-click: a pulse and a ding (a doorbell)
On a heated fluid tank, sounds while powered; use another whistle on it to lower the pitch (it grows), a wrench cycles three octaves; goggles show the note
A redstone pulse makes a Mechanical Crafter grid craft a recipe that doesn't fill every crafter

A station gives a comparator signal while a train is there; a redstone signal forces a train signal red; a Train Observer (select a track, place it nearby) pulses when a train passes, filterable by cargo; schedules can wait for "Station Powered" or a Redstone Link channel

Packager: a pulse packs; Redstone Requester: each pulse sends its order; Re-Packager works while powered; Stock Link: full power stops it sharing, a weaker signal lowers its priority; a Factory Gauge can power a Redstone Link when stock reaches its target, and a receiving link can pause the gauge

A machine's load = its stress impact x RPM, so doubling speed doubles its load; a source gives capacity x RPM. Impact per RPM: press and each crushing wheel 8; mixer, millstone, saw, drill, deployer, pump, bearings, pistons, pulleys, turntable, backtank charging 4; fan, crafter, arm, ejector 2; chain conveyor, cuckoo clock 1; shafts, cogs, gearboxes, belts, clutches, gauges 0. Capacity per RPM: water wheel 32 (256 at its 8 RPM), large water wheel 128 (512 at 4 RPM), hand crank and valve handle 8, windmill 512, steam engine 1024
rows.docs: MISSING (create.md#speed-and-stress explains stress, not the numbers)

rows.how: If load is more than capacity the whole network stops; looking at it shows an "overstressed" hint; add sources or slow the heavy machines
Joining two networks that would turn a shaft in opposite directions or at different speeds breaks the block that joins them; match directions (gearbox, gearshift) first

rows.feature: Only the mixer needs a minimum speed
rows.how: In 6.0.10 only the Mechanical Mixer (and the Display Board) need 30 RPM ("Moderate"); every other machine runs at any speed, just slower. A water wheel's 8 RPM needs two large-to-small cog steps (8 -> 16 -> 32) for a mixer. Top speed for anything is 256 RPM; "Fast" is 100 RPM
rows.docs: WRONG in create.md#speed-and-stress (it says most processing machines need a minimum speed; in 6.0.10 only the mixer and the display board do)

rows.how: Large cog -> small cog doubles, small -> large halves. A Rotation Speed Controller (rotation in along its axis, out to a Large Cogwheel on top) sets an exact RPM on its value box

Gearbox: corners mirror the direction, straight through reverses it. Chain drives pass rotation along a row all in the same direction (a row can turn 90 degrees). Cogwheels side by side turn opposite ways

Right-click a stripped log or stripped wood with Andesite Alloy (andesite casing), a Copper Ingot (copper casing) or a Brass Ingot (brass casing); a Sturdy Sheet on Brass Casing makes Train Casing. JEI lists these as "Manual Item Application"; a deployer can do it

Right-click a shaft or cogwheel with Andesite or Brass Casing to encase it (JEI hides encased versions because this is the only way to make them). On an encased cog a wrench toggles which faces connect; parts added after encasing don't connect until you do. Copper Casing on a fluid pipe locks its connections
One side touching flowing water is enough (more sides add nothing). The Large Water Wheel turns half as fast with twice the total capacity. Right-click with planks to change its wood

Windmill Bearing + a glued structure with at least 8 sail-like blocks (Sails and Sail Frames stick to each other and to blocks without glue; wool needs Super Glue); +1 RPM per 8 sails; right-click the bearing to start or stop (and to edit); value box sets the direction

Engines go on a fluid tank boiler; click an engine with a shaft to make its output. The boiler needs water pumped in, heat (fed blaze burners under it: heated = 1, super-heated = 2) and size; each boiler level lets one more engine run at full power; goggles show Boiler Status (heat, water, size). An unfed blaze burner, magma blocks, lava, campfires or fire underneath give only "passive" heat. Pack: Smithing 35 to make

Hand crank: hold right-click to turn it one way, sneak + hold for the other; it costs hunger. Valve handle: each right-click turns by its set angle (value box), sneak for the other way (a bearing turned this way must be set not to disassemble)

Right-click two shafts with a Mechanical Belt (2 to 20 blocks; flat, 45-degree diagonal or vertical); sneak + right-click cancels a selection; extra shafts can go along it (wrench removes them); belts cost no stress. Take items off with an empty-hand right-click; dye a belt; encase it with casing (wrench removes it)

Placed normally a funnel pulls from the inventory it's on; place it while sneaking to push into it; a wrench flips it; on a belt it takes off or puts on depending on the belt's direction. Redstone stops it. Funnels never move items straight between two containers: put a chute or belt between
Andesite funnels move one item at a time; Brass funnels move up to a stack, with a filter slot and an amount (hold right-click on the filter)
Funnels also work on belts, depots, item drains and upward saws
Over a belt, with belts or funnels at its sides: splits exactly one item off each passing stack to the side; the rest carries on
A filter slot on every open side: filters on inbound sides block other items, filters on outbound sides sort by type. Right-click it to take back the stack it is distributing

Value box: Split (even shares, skips full outputs), Forced Split (waits for them), Round Robin (whole stacks in turn), Forced Round Robin, Prefer Nearest, Randomize, Synchronize Inputs (lets items through only when every tunnel in the group has one, so parallel belts stay in step). Tunnels on side-by-side belts form a group; items can be inserted into a tunnel directly

Move items down between inventories; an Encased Fan at the top or bottom moves them up (goggles show the direction); a chute placed against another's side runs diagonally; wrench adds a window; Industrial Iron encases it. Smart Chute: filter and stack size, redstone stops it
A one-stack "belt" that machines work on (press, deployer, spout, fan) and arms take from; right-click to put an item on or take it off

Sneak + right-click the target spot with the ejector, then place it; with rotation it launches items to that spot (up to 32 blocks, any height, not off to the side). Value box: fire only at a set stack size; it waits for room when aimed at an inventory; redstone stops it; an observer sees each launch
A Brass Tunnel on "Prefer Nearest" with a Weighted Ejector on its side output set to N splits exactly N items off each stack

Before placing: hold the arm and right-click its targets (blue = take from; click again for yellow = put into; left-click to drop one); range 5 blocks; then place it. Without targets it says "No Targets". Cyber Goggles keeps the selection if you switch items (on)

Value box: Round Robin, Forced Round Robin, Prefer First (in the order you picked). Arms don't filter: a Brass Funnel target passes its filter to the arm, and the arm won't pick up what it can't deliver. Targets include belts, depots, funnels, chutes, saws, crafters, basins, blaze burners, jukeboxes, composters, campfires (Ponder tag "Targets for Mechanical Arms")

Right-click to open; put items (or other filters) in. Allow-List (empty lets nothing pass) or Deny-List (empty lets everything pass); Respect Data (durability, enchantments, contents must match) or Ignore Data

Right-click to open; put a reference item in and pick attributes it has: can be smelted / smoked / blasted / washed / crushed / haunted, is enchanted (with X, at max level), is damaged, can be eaten, is placeable, can't stack, has a custom name, is tagged X, was added by mod X, contains fluid X, is dyed X, shulker box empty / partly / full, book author or copy. Allow-List (All), Allow-List (Any) or Deny-List; "Add opposite attribute" adds the "not" form
Matches packages by address (* wildcard); use in funnels, tunnels and arms to route packages

Acts on the spot 2 blocks in front (a block directly in front doesn't block it): places blocks, uses items, clicks blocks, harvests, attacks mobs. Right-click its front to give it an item (or feed it automatically). Wrench toggles Use (right-click) and Punch (left-click) mode

With a filter set it only works while holding a matching item, only accepts matching items and only gives up others. Items it picks up must be pulled out (funnel, hopper) or it stops ("Deployer cannot activate"). Mobs it hits fight back, except creepers (server default)
Over a belt or a depot it holds and applies its item to what's below (casings, sandpaper, sequenced-assembly steps); a redstone signal pauses it after the current cycle

Presses items on a depot, a belt or dropped under it (ingots to sheets), one item at a time (bulk pressing off). Over a Basin it compacts: any 2x2 or 3x3 single-ingredient crafting recipe plus Create's own; its filter slot settles a clash between recipes

Over a Basin: any shapeless crafting recipe plus Create's mixing (brass, andesite alloy, chocolate...), and potion brewing; heated or super-heated recipes need a blaze burner under the basin; its filter slot settles a recipe clash. Needs 30 RPM

After a step a basin puts the result into an inventory, belt or depot below it or diagonally below (an output spout shows when there is one). With nowhere to go it keeps results inside (useful to reuse them as ingredients); then pull them out with a filtered funnel so you don't take the inputs too

Feed it any furnace fuel (by hand, arm or deployer) = Heated; a Blaze Cake = Super-Heated; heat fades as fuel runs out (Cyber Goggles shows time left); a comparator reads heat. An empty burner lit with flint and steel heats no basin (it still works as a fan's smoking or, soul-lit, haunting catalyst)

Air through a block in front of the fan: lava or a fed blaze burner = Bulk Blasting (smelting); fire, a lit campfire or an unfed / flint-lit blaze burner = Bulk Smoking (food); flowing water = Bulk Washing; soul fire, a lit soul campfire or a soul-lit burner = Bulk Haunting. Campfires don't spread fire

Food in a blasting stream burns to nothing: smoke food instead. Fan speed changes only the reach (up to 20 blocks at top speed), never the time (7.5 s). It works on items lying in the stream, on belts and on depots. Air passes through bars, fences, leaves, campfires and sail frames
Fans push or pull mobs and dropped items up to 20 blocks (players too, see Movement & travel); a Nozzle in front spreads the effect all round. Smoking and blasting streams hurt mobs (mob farms)

Crushing raw ore gives 1 crushed ore + 75% chance of an Experience Nugget, not more metal. Washing crushed ore gives 9 nuggets (one ingot) plus a bonus: iron 75% redstone, copper 50% clay, gold 50% quartz, zinc 25% gunpowder. Only ore blocks (Silk Touch) give extra: iron, gold and zinc ore 1 + 75%, copper ore 5 + 25%, redstone ore 6-7, lapis 10-11, diamond and emerald ore 1 + 75%
rows.docs: WRONG in create.md#processing (it says crushing gives more ingots per ore: only true for silk-touched ore blocks)

rows.how: Crushing: gravel -> sand (+ flint, clay), netherrack -> cinder flour, blaze rod -> 3-6 blaze powder, wool -> string, obsidian -> powdered obsidian (sturdy sheets), glowstone and amethyst blocks back to dust and shards. Washing: gravel -> flint / iron nuggets, red sand -> gold nuggets, soul sand -> quartz / gold, sand -> clay, ice -> packed ice

A Spout pours 25 mB of potion onto Cinder Flour (crushed netherrack): Strength -> redstone, Night Vision -> glowstone dust, Harming -> gunpowder (fuel for the schematicannon). Dirt + 500 mB water -> grass block. (The potions must be brewed by a player: the mixer brews only with Brewing-1 ingredients here)

Millstone: power it from the side with a cog, put items in the top, right-click to take results (or extract them); simpler and slower (wheat -> flour, cobblestone -> gravel, gravel -> flint every time, flowers -> dye). Crushing Wheels: a pair turning into each other; drop items onto the gap or insert from the top

An upward saw processes items (stripping and planks, every stonecutter recipe); results move against the saw's rotation; it works in line with a belt; if an item has several results set the filter, or it cycles through them. One item at a time (bulk cutting off)

Place crafters in the recipe's shape; wrench each one's front so the arrows meet at one exit; results go into the inventory at the exit; right-click a front to insert by hand; it crafts once every slot on the path is full. Slot Covers make a crafter count as empty; wrench the backs of crafters to join their inventories so one funnel feeds all

A belt line of deployers, presses, saws and spouts working on one item in order; the item's tooltip shows "Next:" and "Progress"; some recipes repeat the sequence (precision mechanism 5 times) and a share comes out as random salvage. Create JEI Compat pages recipes over 6 steps (scroll or arrow keys); Cyber Goggles lists what the salvage can be
rows.mod: Create, Create JEI Compat, Create: Cyber Goggles

rows.how: Hold Sand Paper with the item in your off-hand (or look at it on the floor) and hold right-click to polish it (rose quartz -> polished rose quartz); a deployer holding sand paper does it on a belt

A Mechanical Pump pushes fluid in its arrow's direction (a wrench reverses it, the rotation doesn't), up to 16 blocks each side; faster = more flow; pumps in one network add up if they face the same way. Pipes only connect endpoints, they never hold fluid. Wrench a straight pipe for a window (windowed pipes don't connect sideways)
An open pipe end pulls up a fluid source block in front of it (or places one when pushing); it fills or drains any fluid container it touches
Smart Fluid Pipe: right-click its filter with a bucket or bottle to pass only that fluid (at a source it picks what to pull). Fluid Valve: rotation one way opens it, the other closes it

Join them: base up to 3x3, up to 32 high, 8 buckets per block; pipes connect on any side; wrench toggles the window; a comparator reads it. In survival you can't fill or empty a tank by hand: use a spout, item drain or basin
