rows.feature: The shoulder view is the third F5 press
rows.how: F5 cycles first person, third person behind, third person front, over-the-shoulder, then first person again. The vanilla views stay in the cycle because replace_default_perspective is false. The pack starts you in first person (the mod's own default starts over the shoulder), and the last view is remembered between sessions.
Bind "Enter Shoulder Surfing", "Enter First Person" or "Enter Third Person (Back/Front)", or their "Toggle ..." versions. All are unbound: Controls > Key Binds > Shoulder Surfing.

In the shoulder view the camera turns on its own. WASD moves relative to the camera and your body turns to face where it walks. You turn to the crosshair when you use an item, interact with or pick a block (always), and when you attack something under the crosshair (only with a target). "Toggle Camera Coupling" (unbound) locks camera and body together, as in vanilla.

In the shoulder view: arrow keys move it left, right, in and out; Page Up/Down move it up and down. Default is 0.75 to the side and 4 blocks back, and it pulls in by itself near walls (dynamic offsets).

rows.feature: Swap shoulder and free look need a key
rows.how: The pack unbinds Swap Shoulder (mod default U, which is the waypoint key) and Free Look (mod default Left Alt, Create's toolbox key). Bind them to use them. Free Look: hold it to look around while you keep walking straight.

rows.feature: Your model fades when the camera is blocked
rows.how: In third person you turn see-through when something is between you and the camera, and you hide when the camera gets too close. If a shader pack draws you oddly, turn "Adjust player transparency" off in Mods > Shoulder Surfing Reloaded > Config (needs a restart).

Mods > Shoulder Surfing Reloaded > Config: camera offsets and presets, FOV override, crosshair type and visibility per view, "Temporary first person in constrained spaces" (off), "Turn camera with player" (off).

rows.feature: Zoom with Z, scroll for more
rows.how: Hold Z to zoom 4x (base FOV factor 0.25). Roll the mouse wheel while holding to zoom further in or back out (0.05 per notch). The level you scrolled to is kept for next time. Works in third person, and mouse sensitivity slows to match.
The spyglass gets the same scroll-wheel zoom and deeper zoom.

The mod puts an options button on the pause screen (the pack's ESC menu places other mods' buttons in its free slots or tray), or use Mods > Just Zoom. Options: smooth zoom, cinematic camera while zooming, hide arms, mouse sensitivity matching (on), zoom in the mirrored F5 view.
` toggles walking forward. Press it again, or S, to stop. An icon shows at the bottom right while it's on.

Mods > Duper's AutoWalk > Config (its "Open Configuration" key is unbound): icon position and size, and feedback as HUD icon, chat message or none. The pack moved the icon from top-left, where it covered the minimap.

rows.feature: Nether portals lead back where you came from
rows.how: The mod remembers which portal you used. Go back through the same portal and you come out of the one you entered, not a neighbour's. The 8:1 ratio stays.
In any waystone or warp stone menu, the "Sort:" button cycles Manual, By Name and By Distance.
Menu > Manage: drag to reorder; double-click moves one to the top, Shift + double-click to the bottom. "Hide Waystone" takes one off your list without forgetting it.

rows.feature: Your own name, favourite and group
rows.how: Menu > Personal Settings, per waystone: an alias only you see, Favorite (puts it in the Favorites group) and a group. Manage Groups lets you make your own groups (label colour, icon) and hide built-in ones: Favorites, Global Waystones, Villages, Player Homes, Dungeons, Resource Sites, Community Hubs, per dimension, Players, Teams. Which built-in groups fill themselves is unverified.
Hold Shift and click a waystone's delete button in the list: it leaves your list until you touch it again. On a global waystone this removes it for everyone, which only admins can do.

Placing a waystone opens its edit screen (name, visibility). To edit it later, sneak + right-click it with an empty hand. A waystone a player placed can only be edited by its owner (restrictedWaystones = PLAYER). Found village and wild waystones aren't restricted, so anyone can rename them (unverified in game).

Edit screen > visibility: "Visible upon Activation" (default: others must find it and touch it) or "Visible to Team". "Visible to Everyone" (global) is admin-only here. "Team" means vanilla scoreboard teams (/team, which only admins can set up), not FTB Teams parties (from the jar).

Warp stone and scrolls: hold right-click for 1.6 s (32 ticks); let go early and nothing happens. Warp plate: stand on it for 0.75 s. After arriving on a plate, step off for 1 s before it sends you again.
Waystones, warp stones and scrolls have no cooldown here. Only the inventory warp button would have one, and it is off (inventoryButton is empty).
Animals on a lead warp with you, even to another dimension (transportLeashed ENABLED). Tamed pets that just follow you stay behind (transportPets DISABLED). Withers never warp.

Right-click an empty warp plate with a shard to put the shard in. Sneak + right-click with an empty hand pops it out. Plain right-click with an empty hand opens the plate's menu, whose slots take extra shards and modifiers.

rows.feature: Pairing warp plates: one way per shard
rows.how: Put a dormant shard in plate A: after 1.5 s it becomes an attuned shard for A and pops out. Put it in plate B, and B sends to A. For the trip back, attune a second dormant shard in B and put it in A. (From the jar; unverified in game.)
Extra attuned shards in a plate's slots make it pick a destination at random each time. Add a quartz to cycle through them in order. A spider eye makes it use crumbling (single-use) shards first.
Each amethyst shard in a plate's slots cuts the stand time by 1.6%; slime balls lengthen it (at most double).

A deepslate shard (pack recipe: compacting cobbled deepslate + flint) locks a plate: it never sends anyone, but other plates' shards still bring people to it. A crumbling attuned shard is used up by its next teleport.

Sneak + right-click your waystone > Manage Modifiers. Items in its slots affect everyone who arrives there. Feather: Slow Falling, 1 s each, up to 8 s. Magma cream: Fire Resistance, 1 s each, up to 8 s. Blaze powder: sets them on fire, 1 s each. Poisonous potato, ink sac and wither rose: Poison, Blindness and Wither, 1 s per item. Milk bucket or honey block: clears their effects. Each diamond raises the effect level, up to 4. Use it as a safe landing pad, or as a trap for whoever finds your waystone.
Hold right-click with a twinbound feather while looking at a friend within 2 blocks for 1 s. The friend then appears in your waystone menu under Players (the exact flow is unverified).
No entity radar (no mobs, players or items on either map) and no cave or underground maps. The server enforces this; the settings read "Disabled by fair-play mode enforced by the server!"
The map tracks nobody: everyone_tracks_everyone is off, and Xaero doesn't read FTB Teams. Share a waypoint or coordinates to meet up.

J opens New Waypoint at your position (the pack's key; the mod's B is the backpack). Fields: name, initials (the letters drawn on the map), colour, X/Y/Z, set, and type: Enabled, Disabled (hidden), Temporary (gone when you leave the server) or Destination (deleted when you reach it). Visibility: Local (only within the max distance), Global (always) or World Map only.

Keypad + drops a temporary waypoint at your feet with no screen (checked in the jar). It vanishes when you leave the server and shows at any distance (Global Temporary Waypoints is on). No keypad on your keyboard? Rebind it.

Each death leaves a skull "Latest Death" waypoint where you died, which is where your grave and dropped Heart are. Older ones become "Old Death" waypoints (kept). A deathpoint deletes itself once you're within 4 blocks of it.

U (or ESC > Waypoints): add/edit, delete, disable/enable, sort (name, initials, distance, angle, colour, reversed), filter box. Also waypoint sets (New Waypoint Set; the Switch Waypoint Set key is unbound), other dimensions' waypoints from the top-right dropdown, Transfer between sets and worlds, and editing several selected waypoints one by one or all at once.

U > select > Share. It asks you to confirm sharing with EVERYONE, then posts it in public chat, where others click [Add]. There is no team-only share, so on a PvP server never share your base: /msg the coordinates instead. The world map's right-click "Share Location In Chat" works the same for any spot.
The waypoint "Teleport" button and the map's "Teleport Here" send /tp, which players don't have on this server, so they fail. Use waystones.

Waypoints show in the world with name and distance. Distance shows for the one nearest your crosshair; "Multiple Waypoint Distances" shows more. The "Toggle In-World Waypoints" and "Toggle On-Map Waypoints" keys are unbound.
Waystones you've activated, sharestones and global waystones appear as waypoints by themselves.

rows.feature: Hide or restore a waystone waypoint
rows.how: Deleting a waystone waypoint only hides it; Y > Waypoint Settings > "Show Deleted 3rd-Party WPs" shows them again. "Discovered Waystone Waypoints" and "Other Waystone Waypoints" turn them off entirely.

M: drag to pan; wheel to zoom (Ctrl + wheel for fine steps). Right-click the map for: Create Waypoint, Set Temporary Waypoint, Open Waypoint Menu, Share Location In Chat, Teleport Here (fails here), Export Map as PNG, Open Settings. Hold right-click and drag to select an area.
With the world map open, J makes a waypoint at the cursor and Keypad + a temporary one there.

rows.feature: Right-click a waypoint on the map
rows.how: Edit, Disable/Enable, Delete (click again to confirm), Share Waypoint In Chat, Teleport (fails here).
The world map shows the cursor's coordinates and biome name; use it to find biomes from the wiki's biome pages. Right-clicking a spot also shows its distance (Display Map Distances).
The icon at the bottom right of the world map lists waypoints with a name filter; hovering highlights one on the map, and clicking jumps there. The hop field takes "X Z" + Enter to jump the view.
The world map's dimension button (Shift-click goes backwards), or the unbound "Toggle Dimension" key, shows the Overworld, Nether or End map from anywhere.

rows.feature: The map only shows where you've been
rows.how: It draws chunks you have loaded and is saved on your PC per server (game folder, xaero/). Footsteps show your recent path.

Y: size, shape (square or circle), Lock Minimap North (an arrow instead of a turning map), zoom (or bind the unbound Zoom In/Out Minimap keys), block colours, opacity, frame, compass, Hide When Under Screen. "Toggle Minimap" (unbound) hides it. UI Scale sets its size; the pack's HUD Layout editor moves it.

Y > Information Settings > Info Display Manager: drag to reorder and turn lines on. Coordinates is on. Others: Overworld Coordinates (in the Nether, where you'd be in the Overworld), chunk coordinates, facing angles, dimension, biome, weather, light level, game time, real time.
"Enlarge Minimap" is unbound in the pack (its Z is Just Zoom). Bind it and hold for a bigger map. Y settings can make it a toggle, centre it, or zoom out while enlarged.

Bind "Toggle Chunk Grid" to draw chunk borders on the minimap. Useful for anything that goes by chunk, such as Create Ore Excavation's veins ("hidden per chunk", PACK_DESIGN.md) and chunk-aligned farms.
Bind "Toggle Light Overlay": it marks blocks at block light 0-7 (where mobs can spawn) on the minimap. Held-torch light from LambDynamicLights doesn't count. It slows the game, so don't leave it on.
"Toggle Slime Chunks" needs the world seed, which the server keeps secret (/seed isn't allowed).

rows.feature: The map picks the right world itself
rows.how: The mod is on the server, so map selection is automatic ("Server" mode). Right Shift (Quick Manual Confirmation) is only needed if it ever says "World map needs confirmation!".
The crosshair is static. While you aim a bow, crossbow or throwable, a second marker shows the first block in your shot's way (obstruction indicator, up to 20 blocks).
Players holding a torch, lantern or other light item, or on fire, light up the area around them on your screen, and yours shows on theirs. In a dark cave a held torch announces you.
A heartbeat plays at 3 hearts (6 health) or less, and your stomach growls at 3 food or less.

An observer facing a waystone pulses when a player activates it for the first time; later uses don't trigger it (from the jar). Wire it to a bell or note block to learn when someone finds your hidden waystone.

rows.feature: Redstone switch for a warp plate
rows.how: Put a redstone torch in a warp plate's slots. From then on, a redstone signal into the plate turns it off.

rows.feature: Warp plates carry items and mobs
rows.how: A warp plate sends any entity standing on it to its target, dropped items and mobs included (not withers). A chute or funnel dropping items onto a plate sends them to the paired plate. (From the jar; unverified in game. waystones.md's "not freight" holds for waystones, not for plates.)

Entity Culling hides what the camera can't see; rope and hose pulleys and Create contraptions are already on its whitelists. If something Create-made still pops out of view, bind "Debug toggle culling" to switch culling off and check.

Holding a torch, lantern, glowstone or other light block, in either hand, lights the area around you. Dropped light items and burning or glowing mobs light up too; torches go dark underwater. It's on your screen only: the real light level doesn't change, so mobs still spawn and crops don't grow. Place torches to make an area safe.

Video Settings > LambDynamicLights tab, or the Mods list: mode Fancy/Fast/Off, which entities glow, creepers glowing before they blow (simple), TNT (off). "Toggle First-Person Lighting" (unbound) turns off only your own held light.

Video Settings > Sodium Extra > Extras: Show FPS (off by default; "extended" adds average and 1% lows), Show Coordinates, Overlay Corner. The corner defaults to top-left, where the voice group heads also sit.
Video Settings > Sodium Extra > Extras: Toasts, or just Advancement, Recipe, System or Tutorial toasts.
Video Settings > Sodium Extra > Render: Player Name Tag, Item Frame Name Tag. This only changes what you see.

Launcher > Mods. Optional and on by default: Shoulder Surfing, Just Zoom, Simple Voice Chat, Chat Heads, LambDynamicLights, Particle Rain, Subtle Effects, Visuality, Falling Leaves, AmbientSounds, 3D Skin Layers, Wavey Capes, Ixeris. First-person Model is optional and off.
Turn on First-person Model in the launcher's Mods page (it's off by default). In game, F6 switches between it and vanilla hands (per its Modrinth page; unverified).

Others see you eat and drink, climb ladders, crawl, row boats, hold reins, swing a held lantern, shiver when freezing, and see the map in your hand (if they've seen that map). Sneak while looking at a tamed wolf or cat to pet it; the hug animation is off. Change it all in Mods > Not Enough Animations.

The Fresh Animations resource pack is on by default (needs EMF/ETF): mobs blink, breathe and look around. Turn it off in Options > Resource Packs for vanilla mobs or a few frames. ETF's settings button is on the resource pack screen.
The hat, jacket and sleeve layers of skins are drawn in 3D up to about 14 blocks away. Per-part toggles: Mods > 3D Skin Layers.
Capes, including the pack's earned capes, bend and sway. Style and wind: Mods > Wavey Capes.
Rain and snow fall as wind-blown particles; deserts and badlands get sandstorms; mist after rain; ripples on water. /particlerain opens its settings (the rain haze effects are off by default).

Sparks from fires and torches, snoring sleepers with Zs, slime trails, dust clouds, fluff from shorn sheep and more. Each one has a switch in Mods > Subtle Effects (a Fzzy Config screen), plus a particle render distance.

Wind, birds, cave and water ambience follow Minecraft's Music & Sounds > Ambient/Environment slider (checked in the jar). /cmdclientconfig opens AmbientSounds' own settings; /ambient-debug shows what's playing.
Neither has a settings screen: edit config/visuality/config.toml or config/fallingleaves-client.toml, or switch them off in the launcher. Falling Leaves also drops leaves from player-placed leaves.

The first time you press V, a setup guide asks for microphone, speaker and activation method; until you finish it the HUD says "Press V to set up". Push to talk is the default method but has no key, so pick one in the guide (or Key Binds > Voice Chat > Push to Talk). With voice activation you start muted after the guide: press O to unmute.

V > Settings: activation method, Voice Activation Threshold, a microphone test button (hear yourself), noise suppression and automatic gain (both on), microphone and speaker choice, 3D audio (Normal/Reduced/Off).

Normal voice reaches 48 blocks, with 3D direction. Hold Whisper (unbound) for 24 blocks; in push-to-talk mode holding Whisper also opens the mic. Everyone in range hears you, enemies too, so use an isolated group for private talk.
O mutes your microphone (the pack's key; the mod's M is the map). You can't mute in push-to-talk mode; just let go. N disables voice entirely: you hear nobody and can't talk.
Icons by name tags and on your HUD show who is talking or whispering, a muted mic, voice disabled, and "not connected" (no voice mod, e.g. switched off in the launcher, or UDP blocked).

V > Group (the pack unbinds the Group key; the mod's G is Curios). Type a name, add an optional password and pick a type, then Create. Normal: outsiders can't hear you, but you hear them. Open: both ways. Isolated: neither. Members' heads show top-left with the speaker outlined. Leave from the same screen.

Others pick the group from V > Group (asked for the password, if set). Invite with /voicechat invite <player> or from the Social Interactions screen (P); the invitee clicks ACCEPT in chat. Also /voicechat join <group> [password] and /voicechat leave.
V > Settings > Adjust Volumes: search a name and drag their volume. 0% mutes them for you; over 100% amplifies. "Other" covers other voice sources.
A button in the V menu, or bind "Hide Voice Chat Icons" (unbound; the mod's H is Missions).
Each player message shows the sender's head. Chat Heads is optional in the launcher.

rows.feature: Far land is built by the server
rows.how: The server builds and sends the far land nobody has visited, gently: 10 requests a second per player, up to 256 chunks out, 250 KB/s each and 1 MB/s in all. Block changes within 128 chunks update live. Admins can pre-build it (dh pregen; PACK_DESIGN.md).

/sparkc profiler start, then /sparkc profiler stop after about 30 s: uploads a report of what your own game spends its time on and gives you the link. Any player can use this client command; /spark on the server is for admins.
Admin-only chunk pre-generation (/chunky radius, /chunky start); players can't use it.

ESC > Settings > Video Settings opens Sodium's options in Reese's layout: a search box and tabs for Sodium (General, Quality, Performance, Advanced), Sodium Extra, Iris, LambDynamicLights, More Culling and other mods.
In Video Settings: hold Shift and scroll over a slider to change it; right-click a cycling button to go backwards; changed options get reset and undo buttons (Reese's options; defaults unverified).
Render distance (Video Settings > General), Distant Horizons' distance, shaders off or Lite, and memory. Then Quality: Leaves Fast, Weather Fast, particles, entity distance, biome blend.

Video Settings > Sodium Extra: animations (water, lava, fire, portals, block animations); particles (all, rain splash, block break, per type); sky, sun, moon and stars; biome and sky colours; cloud height override (192) and distance; beacon beam height limit; armour stands, item frames, paintings, pistons, the enchanting-table book. Its fog options are off while Iris is installed (PACK_DESIGN.md).
Far land reaches 128 chunks (2,048 blocks) by the pack's default, half Distant Horizons' own. Turn it down or off when frames are low.

ESC > Settings: the small Distant Horizons icon button beside the FOV slider, or Mods > Distant Horizons > Config. Quick options: Enable Rendering, LOD Chunk Render Distance Radius, Quality Preset (1 Minimum to 5 Extreme), CPU Load (1 Minimal Impact to 5 "I Paid For The Whole CPU"), Show LOD Gen Progress. faq.md and the pack's config say "Video Settings > Distant Horizons", but the NeoForge jar only adds the FOV-row button (verify in game).

rows.feature: Far land fills in while you stay
rows.how: Far land arrives a few chunks at a time around you. After a fast flight or a long warp you see patches and gaps, which can look like slabs floating over the horizon, until it catches up. It pauses while you move very fast (pauseIfMovingQuickly).

Graphics card and its memory, RAM (6 GB+), CPU threads (CPU Load), and disk: its cache of the server's far land (instance/Distant_Horizons_server_data) reached about 1 GB in one long session. Deleting that folder with the game closed should free the space; the land is sent again (unverified). It also turns vanilla fog off.
Out there only terrain and beacon beams render: no mobs, players or moving contraptions past your normal render distance.
All three shipped shader packs (MakeUp Ultra Fast, Complementary Reimagined, Complementary Unbound) include Distant Horizons programs (checked in the zips), so far land still draws with shaders on.
Launcher > Settings > Graphics: Off, Lite, Balanced or Fancy. In game, K toggles shaders, I opens the pack list and R reloads.

Press I, select a pack, then Apply. "Shader Pack Settings..." holds its options, including a Profile quality preset. Hold Shift and click Reset to reset everything. You can import or export a settings file, drag a shader zip onto the list to add your own, open the shader pack folder, or Hide GUI to preview.
Video Settings (added by Iris): lower Max Shadow Distance for a large FPS gain with shaders, unless the pack sets its own.

rows.feature: The game slows when you look away
rows.how: Alt-tabbed: 1 FPS, 25% volume, toasts held back. Minimised: 0 FPS and silent. Mouse over the window but not focused: 60 FPS. On a laptop on battery, 5 minutes idle drops it to 10 FPS. It's back to normal the moment you click in.

rows.feature: Keep it running in the background
rows.how: Bind "Disable Dynamic FPS (Toggle)" (unbound) for full speed and sound with the window in the background: recording, or watching a farm on a second screen. "Force Unfocused Mode (Toggle)" drops to 1 FPS while you're AFK. Settings: Mods > Dynamic FPS.
Chests, signs, beds, banners, bells, pots, shulker boxes, campfires and lecterns are drawn as terrain for speed. Sign text only shows within 16 blocks; change it in Mods > Better Block Entities.
Item frames past 16 blocks are drawn in a cheaper form; hidden leaf faces, rain and sign text are culled. Settings: Video Settings > More Culling.
Brings back vanilla's darker shading on dirt paths, farmland, slabs and stairs next to full blocks (85% strength by default).
ImmediatelyFast, ModernFix, BadOptimizations and Ixeris only speed things up. Ixeris (mouse input on its own thread) is optional in the launcher if your input misbehaves.
F2 takes one. The folder: Launcher > Settings > Files & repair > Screenshots.

Mods > ReForgedPlay > Config > Recording > Record Server. It's off in the pack; the mod alone records every session. The Replay Viewer is the circling-arrows button at the top right of the title screen panel. Turn recording off again when done: replays get big.

Recording starts by itself when you join (Automatic Recording), and a recording indicator shows on screen. The ESC menu should get Pause/Stop Recording buttons in its mod-button tray (placement unverified). When you leave, a dialog asks you to name the replay.
instance/replay_recordings holds replays; instance/replay_videos holds rendered videos.

Replay Viewer > pick one > Load. P plays and pauses; use the speed slider and the timeline; fly the camera freely. B opens Player Overview (hide players, or spectate one); M adds an event marker; Q is Quick Mode for fast skipping; Z toggles lighting.

I adds a position keyframe and O a time keyframe; a path needs at least 2 of each. H previews the path, C clears it, X opens keyframe presets, V syncs the timeline. J and L roll the camera; K levels it.

Render, in the viewer, sets resolution, framerate, bitrate, a format (MP4, WEBM, MKV, PNG), 360 and stereo modes, and a render queue. Without FFmpeg installed on your PC it stops with "To render a video, you need to have ffmpeg installed".
In the viewer: Edit (insert a cut, or split the replay), Rename, Delete.
Ships and Sable contraptions move in replays recorded with these add-ons; older replays stay frozen. Ships can take a moment to snap into place at the start. Quick Mode works.
The V menu's record button (or the unbound Toggle Recording key) saves voice chat audio as one track per speaker in instance/voicechat_recordings. The server allows recording.

World map > right-click > Export Map as PNG: the whole map or a selected area (hold right-click and drag), with options for night lighting and several unscaled images. Saved under the game folder's xaero directory (exact folder unverified).
